condition: uncomplicated acute unilateral otitis externa ear canal pain after swimming
level_rationale: Two days of unilateral right ear pain and external auditory canal swelling after swimming with new ear discharge today describes uncomplicated acute otitis externa requiring non-emergent outpatient clinic examination and prescription topical otic therapy, whereas acute drooping on the right side of the face alongside right ear canal inflammation signals cranial nerve VII palsy or complicated necrotizing infection requiring immediate ER care.

Developed discharge from the right ear today

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + single-fact acute symptom escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Four atomic reference facts cover recent swimming 3 days ago, 2 days of right ear pain, 2 days of right ear canal swelling, and new right ear discharge today, with a 2-word span difference (20 vs 22 words) and 8 identical trailing tokens ('today so I need to go to the'). Replacing atomic fact f4 with ipsilateral right facial droop escalates care from outpatient clinic (level 2) to ER (level 4) with zero stated negatives.
